title: Phoenix
tagline: The lander that touched ice in the Martian arctic.
mystery: Is there water hiding under the soil of Mars?
p1.launch: 4 August 2007. Phoenix leaves Earth. Ten months and 681 million km later...
p1.hello: I'm Phoenix! I've come to the cold north of Mars, where the ice is.
p1.where: 25 May 2008. The arctic plains of Mars: farther north than anyone had landed.
p1.how: Parachute first, then eight little thrusters. Feet down, engines off!
p1.call: Earth was so far away that my 'I'm down!' took about 15 minutes to arrive.
p2.wait: First, I wait 15 minutes for the dust to settle.
p2.body: Three legs, an eight-sided body, and two eight-sided solar wings.
p2.look: Flat ground with pebbles and long troughs. No big rocks, no hills.
p2.days: Within four days: a 360-degree panorama, my 2.5 m arm out, and weather reports.
p3.ice: Water ice is found in the polar regions. Let's dig and look!
p3.hint: Hold the button to scoop the soil with the arm.
p3.dug: Look, bright clumps in the bottom of the trench!
p3.bright: Are they salt? Or ice? Let's watch them for a few days.
p3.vanish: They vanished in four days, into the thin air. It was water ice!
p4.lab: On my deck: tiny ovens, and a lab that mixes soil with water from Earth.
p4.hint: Tap an instrument, then hold until the bar is full.
p4.s.tega: The ovens heated a sample, and found water. NASA said it: there is water on Mars!
p4.s.meca: The soil is alkaline and salty, with sodium, magnesium, chloride and potassium.
p4.win: And a surprise: perchlorate in the soil!
p4.life: Perchlorate could be food for microbes, and useful one day for human explorers.
p5.sun: Up here in summer, the Sun never set. Not until August!
p5.goal: How long did I keep working?
p5.win: 161 days, from landing to my very last signal!
p5.extended: My 90-day mission was done by the end of August, and extended to 30 September.
p6.dark: Then summer ended. Less sunlight, less power, every day.
p6.last: 2 November 2008. My last signal, before my power ran out.
p6.bye: I found the ice. Now I sleep in the cold north. Goodbye!
